item.title: TencentDB Agent Memory
item.description:
The Problem
AI agents waste time repeating work across sessions. Each new conversation restarts from zero—re-reading docs, re-discovering workflows, and re-explaining context. When multiple agents work on the same project, there is no shared memory layer, so knowledge silos form and teams lose institutional learning.
What This Does

item.title: openwiki
item.description:

This can lead to outdated or incomplete documentation, making it difficult for developers to understand the code and for users to effectively utilize the software.

item.title: UpSnap
item.description:
The Problem
Managing Wake-on-LAN (WoL) for multiple machines typically requires either command-line tools, dedicated hardware, or manual ARP table lookups. Teams managing fleets of headless or remote servers need a centralized, web-accessible way to wake, ping, and optionally shut down machines without SSH access to each one.

item.title: cloudflare os
item.description:
The Problem
Enterprises struggle to give non-technical employees safe, productive access to AI agents. Most solutions either lock down functionality so tightly that agents are useless, or open access so broadly that data leaks become inevitable. Companies need a way to let employees build custom tools and automate workflows without creating security nightmares.

item.title: WorldGrow
item.description:

This agent treats context as variables and tools like recursive subagents as function calls, allowing for more efficient and programmatic management of tasks.

item.title: emexDE
item.description:
The Problem
iOS developers who need to write, compile, and test native code while away from a Mac have no viable option. Xcode requires macOS, cloud-based solutions need connectivity, and on-device editors can't compile native binaries. This forces developers to carry laptops or delay work until they're at a desk.
What This Does

item.title: shepherd
item.description:
The Problem
Agent runs are black boxes. When an agent writes files, calls APIs, or modifies state, there is no way to inspect, roll back, or replay that execution. Debugging requires re-running from scratch, and supervision requires trusting the agent's output without review. Docker containers are too slow for checkpointing, and Git snapshots capture only files, not execution state.
What This Does
Shepherd records agent execution as a reversible, Git-like trace. The core mechanism lives in co...

item.title: winboat
item.description:
The Problem
Running Windows applications on Linux has historically required either dual-booting, maintaining a full virtual machine with a separate desktop, or relying on compatibility layers like Wine that don't support all software. Each approach forces users to choose between convenience and compatibility.
What This Does
WinBoat runs Windows inside a Docker or Podman container as a VM, then uses FreeRDP's RemoteApp protocol to render individual Windows applications as native Linux windows....

item.title: wifui
item.description:
The Problem
Windows users lack a fast, keyboard-driven tool for managing Wi-Fi connections from the terminal. The standard GUI (netsh, Settings app) requires mouse interaction or verbose command-line incantations. Network engineers and developers who live in the terminal need something faster.
What This Does

item.title: mixture of kittens
item.description:
The Problem
Standard Mixture-of-Experts training suffers from serialized compute and communication steps, frequent CPU-GPU synchronizations, and non-deterministic execution. These overheads compound on NVL72 systems where inter-GPU communication latency directly impacts training throughput. Existing solutions leave significant headroom on the table.
What This Does
Mixture-of-Kittens fuses all MoE computation and communication into a single CUDA megakernel (csrc/mok_megakernel.cuh). The kernel...

item.title: posta
item.description:
The Problem
Teams that rely on transactional or marketing email often need to use third-party services like SendGrid or Mailgun, which means sharing sensitive email infrastructure and delivery data with external providers. Self-hosting email delivery typically requires stitching together multiple tools—an MTA, a queue system, a template engine, analytics—and managing deliverability, bounce handling, and security yourself. Posta packages all of this into a single, self-hosted platform.

item.description:
